key_idea: It is a bipartite max flow customers -> stores, but each customer touches up to 2500 stores; route each rectangle through a 2D sparse table of infinite-capacity helper nodes so every customer needs only 4 edges.
sketch: Build nodes (p,q,i,j) for the 2^p x 2^q block at (i,j); each links with infinite capacity to its two halves (halve rows first, then columns) and 1x1 blocks link to the sink with the store inventory. Each customer gets a source edge of capacity x and at most 4 infinite edges to the overlapping blocks covering its rectangle (overlap is harmless for flow). Customers with identical rectangles are merged. About 90k helper nodes and 600k edges; Dinic finishes in well under a second because all augmenting paths are short. Use 64-bit capacities (answer up to 1e14). Stress-tested against a direct-edge max flow on small grids.
